'''''Cistus crispus''''' is a [[shrub]]by [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Cistaceae]], with pink to purple flowers, native to south-western Europe and western north Africa.

==Description==
''Cistus crispus'' grows up to {{convert|50|cm|ftin|abbr=on|0}} tall. Its grey-green leaves are wavy (undulate), oblong to elliptical in shape, usually {{convert|1|–|4|cm|in|abbr=on|1}} long by {{convert|4|–|15|mm|in|abbr=on|1}} wide. They have three prominent veins and are covered a mixture of short stellate hairs and longer simple hairs. The flowers are arranged in few-flowered [[Cyme (botany)|cymes]], each flower being {{convert|3|–|4|cm|in|abbr=on|1}} across with five purplish-red [[petal]]s and five hair-covered [[sepal]]s.<ref name=Warb68/>

==Taxonomy==
''Cistus crispus'' was first described by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1753 in ''[[Species Plantarum]]'' (p. 524).<ref name=TPL_kew-2723349/> The specific epithet ''crispus'' means "curly" or "finely waved", referring to the leaves.<ref name=Coom94p42/>

It hybridizes with ''[[Cistus albidus]]'' to form the hybrid [[Cistus × incanus|''Cistus'' × ''incanus'']].<ref name=GuzmVarg05/>

==Phylogeny==
A 2011 [[Molecular phylogenetics|molecular phylogenetic study]] placed ''C. crispus'' as the deepest branching member of the clade of purple and pink flowered ''Cistus'' species (the "purple pink clade" or PPC).<ref name=CiveLeclDemoAgna11/>

==Distribution==
''Cistus crispus'' is native to north Africa<ref name=GuzmLled09/> and south-western Europe, including [[Portugal]], [[Spain]], [[France]], [[Corsica]], [[Italy]] and [[Sicily]].<ref name=Warb68/>
